#5149. One Bitcoin miner paid an $11.9M tariff bill four years after delivery

Bitcoin mining companies are still resolving customs disputes over machines that entered the US years ago.

Bitcoin miner Bitfarms thought the machines it brought into Washington state in 2021 had been made in Malaysia. Its supplier said so, and the company provided US Customs officials with documents supporting that claim.

Four years later, the company paid the government $11.9 million. US Customs and Border Protection had challenged the machines' declared origin, arguing that they were made in China and subject to a 25% import duty.

Bitfarms disputed the assessment, but its financial statements show it paid in October 2025, after Customs told it the duties were required.

The payment shows a cost that can follow a mining company long after its equipment was delivered and started working. Other miners have faced similar disputes over where their machines were made, with one company recently avoiding a potential $100 million assessment and another still contesting an estimate that reached $130 million.

Those numbers don't add up to a single bill for the industry. Each dispute involves different shipments, documents, and decisions, and the outcomes can look very different even when the companies believe they have evidence supporting their declared origins.

Bitfarms' dispute began in early 2022, when Customs challenged the origin of the machines imported the previous year. The company said its Chinese vendor had represented that the equipment came from Malaysia, while Customs asserted that it was manufactured in China.

The miner submitted supporting documents in the third quarter of 2023 and again in the first quarter of 2025. It also paid $180,000 of the duties in 2024, according to its later filing. As of June 2025, management said it didn't consider a future cash outflow probable and hadn't recorded a provision for the dispute.

That was an accounting assessment based on what the company knew at the time. In August 2025, Customs responded that duties were required, and Bitfarms reported the payment two months later.

Bitfarms disclosed $180,000 of customs duties paid in 2024 and a separate $11.9 million payment to Customs in October 2025, including interest. The filing’s stated duties and interest components do not reconcile to its reported October payment.

Source: Bitfarms September 2025 financial statements, customs duties note

The company hasn't disclosed enough to reconstruct every step of the customs process or establish whether it paid under protest. Nonetheless, its filings do show how a dispute over a shipment can remain relevant to a company's finances long after the initial purchase.

Company disclosures trace the disputed origin of mining equipment from its arrival in 2021 to a payment in October 2025.

The purchase year did not determine when Bitfarms would pay the customs assessment.

Based on company disclosures, not the underlying Customs correspondence. The October payment included interest. The filing does not establish every procedural step or whether payment was under protest.

Timeline transcribed from Note 16 of Bitfarms September 2025 financial statements. Dollar figures converted from the stated thousands of US dollars. Milestones are equally spaced for readability, not elapsed time.

Based on company disclosures, not the underlying Customs correspondence. The October payment included interest. The filing does not establish every procedural step or whether payment was under protest.

Bitfarms has since reorganized under Keel Infrastructure and shifted toward AI and high-performance computing. It paid the customs bill before that transition reached a major milestone: Keel stopped its US Bitcoin mining operations in June 2026 as it prepared sites for other uses.

Thanks for signing up to The Catalyst. Look out for your first daily email. If you already receive it, you’re all set.

Other miners have also been shifting power access and data-center sites toward AI, while older import disputes still appear in their financial disclosures.

The money involved can affect how much they have available for equipment and projects, although a disclosed potential charge isn't necessarily money they will have to pay.

Import duties can depend on where a product was made, which sounds simple until a machine contains components from several countries and is assembled elsewhere.

US customs forms ask importers to identify the product's country of origin. When production takes place in more than one country, the answer can depend on where the product underwent its last substantial transformation, according to Customs' entry instructions.

The manufacturing process and supporting records can affect the duty owed. The supplier's certificate can support the declared origin, but Customs can still challenge it.

Equipment can also be released and put to work before Customs resolves every issue. Customs uses a process called liquidation to make its final duty calculation for an entry.

Importers can challenge certain decisions through an administrative protest, but deadlines and exceptions depend on the decision being challenged. The public filings don't establish which procedural rules explain every stage of the miners' disputes.

Selling the equipment doesn't automatically settle an importer's customs obligations either. Federal regulations describe duties as a debt owed by the importer, which can be discharged through payment or applicable legal relief.

That doesn't mean the buyer of a secondhand machine automatically inherits the seller's customs bill, since the importer and the terms of any transaction need to be identified separately.

IREN received a notice in April 2025 concerning hardware it imported between April 2024 and February 2025. Customs asserted that the equipment was of Chinese origin and assessed a 25% tariff, while IREN said the seller and shipping documents supported a different origin.

The company contested an exposure of approximately $100 million. In October 2026, Customs approved its protests and accepted the declared origin of the covered hardware, IREN reported in its September-quarter filing. No additional tariff, administrative fee, or interest is payable for that matter.

The $100 million was an amount IREN had disputed and no longer has to pay for the covered imports. The company hasn't disclosed enough about the decision to establish whether the same reasoning applies to other shipments or other miners.

CleanSpark has had a mixed outcome so far. In its June-quarter filing, submitted in August, the miner said Customs had approved some of its protests over machines imported in 2024, while other entries remained contested.

If Customs prevailed on the remaining entries, CleanSpark estimated that its total tariff liability for the previously purchased machines could reach approximately $130 million, excluding interest. Management considered a loss improbable and recorded no provision as of June 30.

DarkHorse Technologies, previously known as Sphere 3D, faces a smaller claim that shows how an older equipment purchase can appear in the accounts of a miner with a different name and business plan.

In August, Customs notified DarkHorse that it was asserting Chinese-origin duties on machines purchased in 2022 by a subsidiary acquired in the Cathedra Bitcoin combination.

The company says its subsidiary received certificates from the seller supporting a non-Chinese origin, and it filed a protest in September. Its latest quarterly report puts potential liability at up to $2.3 million, including interest, if Customs prevails. DarkHorse has not recorded a liability.

Company estimates if Customs prevails. CleanSpark's was approximately $130 million excluding interest as of June 30. DarkHorse's was up to $2.3 million including interest in its Sept. 30 report. Reporting dates and interest treatment differ.

Source: CleanSpark June 2026 Form 10-Q, Note 15 · DarkHorse September 2026 Form 10-Q, customs duties contingency

DarkHorse is separately selling its legacy mining fleet as it shifts toward AI infrastructure. Its quarterly report estimated $2.9 million in proceeds, with $1.3 million from machines sold by Sept. 30.

Bitfarms reported a payment, IREN's covered assessment has been resolved, CleanSpark's estimate excludes interest, and DarkHorse's includes it. Adding them together would treat a past payment and an avoided charge as outstanding bills.

CleanSpark's remaining protests and DarkHorse's challenge will determine whether either miner faces a further payment on the disputed imports.

IREN's result shows that a challenge can succeed, while Bitfarms' earlier payment shows why investors can't assume that a company's initial accounting assessment will be the final word.

#5147. Solana’s 2027 roadmap promises faster growth, but the market wants proof

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Solana’s core developer, Anza, has unveiled its 2027 roadmap.

Structurally, the roadmap focuses on making Solana faster, more efficient, and capable of handling more activity. The network aims to double its compute capacity and cut the compute units needed for token account transactions by 80%.

It also plans to increase the number of accounts supported in each transaction from 64 to 96 and make it easier to run models fully on-chain.

Naturally, the question becomes whether Solana is preparing for its next growth phase. Interestingly, the previous major network upgrade was also performed by Anza.

This upgrade, called Alpenglow, brought down Solana’s finality time to 150ms from 12.8 seconds, making the network significantly faster.

The result? As the chart above shows, Solana processed over 10 billion transactions in October, keeping monthly activity above that level. However, more than halfway through November, the network has recorded just over 2 billion transactions.

That’s 5x lower than October’s total, suggesting that the recent spike in activity may be losing steam. Given this, it might be too early to expect any bull run in 2027.

In fact, SOL is currently down 20% in October, which indicates that the market hasn’t seen increased demand from improving fundamentals just yet.

So, what does it say about the recent “Anthropic-driven” momentum on Solana [SOL]?

SPCX was first to demonstrate how major IPOs can bring fresh trading activity to Solana.

The launch of SpaceX’s tokenized stock, SPCX, on Solana on the 12th of June brought significant activity to the network.

The token recorded $108 million in 24-hour on-chain trading volume shortly after launch and crossed 10,000 holders within six days, with cumulative trading volume exceeding $350 million.

Notably, a similar trend has emerged following the ANT IPO launch. As the chart below shows, Anthropic’s ANT has generated over $29 million in trading volume on Solana since launch across three issuers. Backpack’s token alone accounted for $26.8 million, or nearly 92% of the total.

This shows how major IPO launches are bringing fresh trading activity to Solana.

Adding to this, DeFiLlama data shows that Solana’s stablecoin market cap has risen nearly 3% in the past 24 hours, pointing to a fresh liquidity inflow after months of weakness.

However, the bigger picture remains mixed.

Despite the rise in on-chain activity and liquidity, SOL is still trading around $70. This suggests that the recent activity has yet to translate into stronger buying pressure.

For Solana’s 2027 roadmap to support a longer-term recovery, the network will therefore need to sustain this growth beyond short-term activity.

Anza’s 2027 roadmap aims to improve Solana’s speed, capacity, and overall network efficiency.

SPCX and ANT have boosted on-chain trading activity, but SOL’s price weakness suggests that stronger demand is still missing.

#5144. A Bitcoin drop toward $53,000 could put $240 million in collateral at risk

An Aave liquidation seized nearly 90 wrapped bitcoin on Saturday. A tracker flagged more collateral across eight pools if lending protocols’ price feeds fall into the $52,700 to $54,300 range.

Bitcoin loan liquidations hit Aave V3 on Ethereum Saturday as Bitcoin fell to about 55,000 USDT on OKX. At 06:16:47 UTC, a liquidator repaid 4,779,047 USDC and took 89.64 WBTC, an Ethereum token tied to Bitcoin that the borrower had pledged as collateral.

The liquidation went through just before the minute in which Bitcoin reached its low on OKX. OKX’s BTC-USDT spot data show a low of 55,277 USDT in the minute that began at 06:16 UTC and 55,134 USDT in the next minute. The exchange’s daily history puts the Nov. 21 low at $55,134. Aave values the collateral behind each loan using oracle prices, the prices fed into the lending protocol.

The transaction’s transfer record shows what happened after the seizure. The liquidator exchanged about 88.14 WBTC for USDC through Bebop and about 1.5 WBTC for wrapped ether on Uniswap V3. The effect on Bitcoin’s spot price remains unmeasured.

DeFi Terminal’s event record covers the USDC liquidation. The decoded Ethereum logs show a separate Aave liquidation in the same transaction that repaid about 3.43 million USDT and transferred another 64.19 WBTC.

A few hours later, ArbitrageX’s lending tracker estimated that $239.8 million in collateral across its sample could become eligible for liquidation in a reference-price range of about $52,700 to $54,300. The estimate used eight pool reads taken at 10:23 and 10:24 UTC on Nov. 21. It covered Aave V3 and Compound V3 on Ethereum, Arbitrum and Base, and Morpho Blue on Ethereum and Base. The positions included several tokenized versions of Bitcoin.

The Nov. 21 exchange low and later Aave WBTC oracle reading sat above ArbitrageX’s modeled liquidation band.

The $239.8 million is modeled exposure. Protocol oracles and loan balances determine when an individual position becomes eligible.

The OKX spot low and later Aave V3 Ethereum WBTC oracle reading are separate observations at different times. The band covers only ArbitrageX’s eight sampled lending pools.

A linear scale from 52,000 to 59,000 plots the published numerical values. The OKX candle is quoted in USDT; the later Ethereum WBTC oracle and model band are quoted in USD. Band endpoints $52,724.76 and $54,326.41 are rounded to the nearest dollar. ArbitrageX sampled eight lending pools at 10:23–10:24 UTC.

The OKX spot low and later Aave V3 Ethereum WBTC oracle reading are separate observations at different times. The band covers only ArbitrageX’s eight sampled lending pools.

The tracker used Aave V3’s Ethereum WBTC oracle reading of $58,175.80 as its reference. In the same snapshot, Aave V3 on Arbitrum valued WBTC at $57,897.05. An exchange trade through the modeled band would be a signal to check those feeds. Each loan’s debt and collateral balances determine whether the price leaves it eligible for liquidation.

On Aave, a position becomes eligible for liquidation when its health factor falls below one. A borrower can raise that measure by supplying more collateral or paying down debt, and Aave’s rules allow a partial liquidation in some cases. On Morpho, the loan-to-value ratio must exceed the threshold set for that market. The estimate from ArbitrageX’s Saturday morning UTC snapshot measures collateral that could become eligible under its assumptions. The amount a liquidator actually receives is recorded when a transaction executes.

The next U.S. inflation and GDP reports give borrowers a reason to watch those prices again on Wednesday. The Bureau of Economic Analysis has scheduled its October Personal Income and Outlays report, which includes the PCE price index, for Nov. 25 at 8:30 a.m. ET. Its second estimate of third-quarter GDP and corporate profits is due at the same time. If the reports shift rate expectations, the two-year Treasury yield can show how traders are repricing the outlook. Any move in Bitcoin’s spot price still needs to reach lending oracles before it changes the collateral values that protocols use.

If oracle prices fall toward the band, look for repayments and extra collateral in the same markets. A smaller estimate alongside those transactions would point to borrowers rebuilding their buffers. A change in the tracker’s coverage or in the mix of positions could also move the estimate, so compare the same pools over time. A wider wave would mean more positions or markets recording confirmed liquidations over comparable periods. The event logs can show how much debt was paid down and how much collateral changed hands.

#5139. Singapore wants to test stablecoin payments by AI agents

The central bank plans to help develop a shared way to verify an agent’s authority. A separate sandbox would test safeguards for payments and corporate treasury.

Singapore’s central bank plans to help develop a common way for banks to verify who an AI agent represents and what the customer has authorized it to do. Chia Der Jiun, managing director of the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS), outlined the proposal on Nov. 19 at the Singapore FinTech Festival. A separate Singapore sandbox would test safeguards for AI agent payments, with stablecoins and tokenized deposits among the options.

Under the proposed know-your-agent protocol, a financial institution would receive information about the agent’s identity, the customer it acts for, its delegated authority and the rules it must follow. The protocol would also convey any assurances about the agent’s origin and reliability. The institution could use that information to set the scope of access and give the agent a dedicated, secure channel.

Chia said the customer’s mandate should specify the actions the agent may take and the limits and conditions on them. The more discretion the agent has or the greater the potential impact, the stronger the controls should be. MAS plans to help develop the protocol in the next phase of its Safeguards for Agentic Finance at Runtime initiative.

MAS and the Future of Finance Institute announced the planned Agentic Money Sandbox on Nov. 18. The institute would set up a controlled environment for institutions to test payments and corporate treasury management with digital money ahead of any live deployment.

Thanks for signing up to The Catalyst. Look out for your first daily email. If you already receive it, you’re all set.

Singapore has proposed a way to check an agent’s authority and separate sandbox trials for payments and corporate treasury.

The proposed payment trial would put the identity and authority checks at the bank or payment provider before execution.

The proposed treasury trial separates the company’s mandate from the bank’s terms for accepting an instruction.

The customer sets the mandate. The bank or payment provider sets controls before acting on an instruction.

MAS plans to help develop the protocol. The diagrams show the proposed trials and examples of digital money.

The arrows show who would pass an instruction to whom under the approach Chia Der Jiun outlined at the Singapore FinTech Festival on Nov. 19. The selectable views compare the two proposed trials.

MAS plans to help develop the protocol. The diagrams show the proposed trials and examples of digital money.

In the proposed payments test, the participating bank or payment provider would verify the agent’s identity and authority and apply risk controls before executing an instruction. Chia cited tokenized deposits and stablecoins as examples of the digital money the trial could use.

In the treasury test, a company would define what its agent could do. The agent could monitor cash balances and upcoming payments, decide when and where funds should move, and use tokenized deposits for permitted transfers. The bank would set its own controls and terms for accepting each instruction.

In a Nov. 18 speech, Singapore Deputy Prime Minister and MAS Chairman Gan Kim Yong gave the example of an agent making a payment under a contract once the relevant terms had been met and checked. The joint release named DBS, OCBC, Standard Chartered and UOB as the institute’s launch partners. The same release gave no sandbox start date or participant list.

Gan said institutions and companies remain accountable for actions taken on their behalf. Chia asked who bears responsibility when an agent makes a mistake or exceeds its mandate.

#5137. The 10 Best Moisturizers for Men in 2026, According to Grooming Experts

Our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

Keep your mug hydrated no matter your skin type—or the temperature.

WHETHER YOU'RE A grooming editor, like me, whose skincare routine is extensive (and seemingly growing every day), or a bare-minimum type of guy, your regimen centers on the same thing: moisturizer. After the face wash, serum, and eye cream, applying moisturizer brings it all home. The only product that should follow is sunscreen in the morning (year-round, please!), so it’s crucial to find one you dig that matches your skin type and budget.

For those who are especially short on time or stubborn about keeping their skincare routine short, there are plenty of quality SPF moisturizers to consider. Regardless, moisturizer is the crux of proper skincare. The third act climax that culminates the impact of all that has preceded it and cements a lingering effect of what follows.

Applying twice a day (once in the morning, once at night) strengthens your skin barrier, locks in hydration, and keeps your complexion healthy and balanced. Of course, not all moisturizers are created equal, and few are effective for all skin types. These are the best available for everybody’s skin.

Neutrogena’s Hydro Boost Face Moisturizer has been in rotation for dermatologist Dr. Alex Zeitany, M.D., since 2015—and it’s the one she consistently recommends to patients looking for serious hydration without the heavy feel. Powered by hyaluronic acid, which holds up to 1,000 times its weight in water, this gel delivers a cool, weightless finish while locking in moisture like a pro, according to Dr. Zeitany.

I’ve applied this before heading out into serious heat (followed by sunscreen, of course), and my skin was never dry or tight, remaining smooth and hydrated for hours. Add in the fact that it could double as the best budget moisturizer at barely over $25, and it’s hard to find a reason against this ultra-hydrating option.

Testing Notes: Like many men, I tend to shy away from moisturizers that leave my skin feeling goopy or greasy, which is why this watery gel rose to the top of the list. The consistency is smooth and silky, and while not completely transparent, it is definitely more of a gel consistency than a cream. It glides onto skin easily and has a slight cooling sensation, but also sinks into your skin quickly without leaving any sort of shine or residue whatsoever.

The formula is packed with hyaluronic acid, one of the most important ingredients in a moisturizer because it is a humectant—meaning it draws moisture from the air—and even with a formula as lightweight as this, my skin still felt healthy and hydrated hours later.

Read More: Best Moisturizers for Dry Skin

As someone with sensitive skin, La Roche-Posay’s moisturizer is a personal favorite thanks to its calming hydration and formula free from fragrance or harsh additives. Dermatologist Dr. Jeremy Brauer, M.D., also swears by it. He notes its blend of prebiotic thermal water, ceramides, niacinamide, and glycerin makes it gentle enough for nearly every skin type, while the richer texture works especially well for men’s skin.

Testing Notes: I have found that moisturizers designed for sensitive skin can often go overboard on thickness because they’re trying to pack as much moisture into the formula as possible. But as one of the best skincare brands for men with sensitive skin, La Roche-Posay knows better. Out of all the sensitive skin moisturizers I’ve tried, this is the best one for wearing during the day and at night because even though it’s thick, it doesn’t feel heavy on my skin and offers a ton of hydration for how lightweight the formula is.

It also heals as well as it hydrates. Within a few days, I noticed red or rough patches on my face smoothing out. Of course, the fragrance-free factor is perfect for sensitive or easily irritated skin, but also for anyone who just doesn’t like fragrance in their products.

Read More: Best Moisturizers for Sensitive Skin

SPF Moisturizers provide sunscreen protection as well as hydration, making them a time-saving skincare product year-round. Marlowe No. 128 offers the best of both worlds: the feel and hydration of a quality facial moisturizer, along with the sun protection of the best sunscreens out there. Despite its high level of SPF, it’s non-comedogenic and doesn’t clog pores. Plus, it comes in a container that’s at least 50 percent recycled. I declared it the best SPF moisturizer for a reason.

Testing Notes: I love Marlowe's lightweight, non-greasy formula and how quickly it absorbed into our skin. Its blend of nourishing and deeply hydrating ingredients like aloe, green tea, and shea butter leaves skin feeling smooth, refreshed, and balanced. Better yet, it’s only $20, and the tube lasts over a month with daily use.

This standby from Kiehl’s is a classic for a reason. It’s creamy but not heavy and suitable for all skin types, even oily skin. It hydrates your skin all day, even in cold weather, but still won’t leave your mug feeling gunky. Style and Reviews Director Christian Gollayan has been using Kiehl's Ultra Facial Cream for nearly a decade, and it has been his go-to moisturizer for traveling.

"It moisturizes my skin without breaking out, and it's ultra-hydrating without clogging my pores," he says. "That's why it's a great travel moisturizer since it hydrates without irritating in almost any climate I've been in."

Testing Notes: In terms of generally all-around perfect everyday moisturizers, this one gets top billing because it just does it all. The cream formula strikes the balance between being lightweight but still super moisturizing, and while it looks heavier than many others on this list, I’ve found that it doesn’t feel that way when you’re wearing it.

It’s also ideal for colder weather because it’s rich enough to protect your skin from the drying cold air, but not occlusive or greasy like some other heavy moisturizers. And while it is suitable for all skin types and for pretty much any climate, if you have especially oily skin, you may want to use only a tiny bit (a little goes a long way with this one).

This lightweight, non-greasy facial moisturizer is suitable for all skin types, but is specifically designed with oily or acne-prone skin in mind. Its formula includes vitamin E, aloe vera, and glycerin, which help soothe and protect the skin while maintaining moisture balance and, crucially, hydrating without clogging pores. With a quick-absorbing application, matte finish, and oil-free formula, it's an ideal everyday option for those with naturally oily skin.

Testing Notes: I can confirm that the Baxter of California Oil Free Moisturizer absorbs absurdly fast and doesn't leave any lingering residue or oil, even on sensitive skin. The chamomile and camellia extract (essentially green tea) also helped reduce redness and any inflammation on my face. Not to mention, it's truly fragrance-free, making it perfect for combining with colognes or other fragranced products without the scents clashing.

Typically, the main benefit and difference of a night cream compared to a daily moisturizer is that night creams are specifically formulated to work with the skin's natural overnight repair process to provide richer hydration, whereas standard moisturizers are generally lighter and designed for daytime use to maintain the skin’s moisture balance.

Harry's Night Lotion, however, offers up the benefits of both in strides. Thanks to ingredients like glycerin and jojoba, Harry's provides deep hydration overnight and replenishes moisture, while its niacinamide also works to improve the skin's texture and soothe irritation.

Testing Notes: Sure, the Harry's Night Lotion bottles are pretty tiny (1.7 oz), but since you only really need one or two dabs to cover your entire face, the bottles last much longer than their size would suggest. Plus, at under $10 a bottle, you'd be hard-pressed to find a cheaper, more effective option. The only caveat is that it does include some fragrance, it's subtle, but could still prove to be an issue for those extra sensitive.

If you’ve ever dealt with facial redness, you’re probably familiar with Tower 28. But the brand has become synonymous with treating inflamed and sensitive skin that’s prone to redness, and this cream is a prime example of why. Backed by hyaluronic acid, ceramides, and lysine, it’s designed specifically for easily irritated skin.

The hyaluronic acid draws in and retains moisture, ceramides repair and strengthen the skin barrier, and lysine supports healing and reduces irritation. It’s also completely fragrance-free and non-comedogenic (meaning it won’t clog your pores), so it’s safe for the most sensitive skin. You get all that for under $25.

Testing Notes: As a lifelong pasty Irishman, I’ve tested many moisturizers designed for redness. There have been others that effectively battle the issue and calm my skin, but none at this price point. And very few have been this easy to use. While the container is on the smaller size (only 1.86 oz), this stuff is pretty thick. Not in the feels cakey on your face or leaves it greasy sense, but that you only need to use a little to cover everything. I’ll get months out of this tiny tube.

A good barrier-supporting cream helps strengthen the skin’s natural protective barrier, locking in moisture and defending against environmental stressors to keep skin healthy, hydrated, and resilient. This K-beauty option is the best you’ll find, at less than the cost of a salad in NYC.

The formula is backed by ceramide NP, which helps strengthen and repair the moisture barrier, while vitamin B5 (aka panthenol) hydrates and soothes dry or irritated skin. It’s topped off with succinic acid, which promotes a healthier skin environment. All that in a $14 package.

Testing Notes: Think of barrier support as essentially your skin’s offensive line, helping to block and protect against outside forces attempting to penetrate your skin. In that sense, this option from Rael proves to be the early 90s Dallas Cowboys—offering Hall of Fame protection. Its Great Wall is boosted by a creamy, quick-absorbing application that leaves my skin feeling smooth and healthy with a clearer complexion.

When the weather gets warmer, thicker moisturizers are going to feel extra-heavy on your skin. This will not only be uncomfortable, but it can also clog your pores and leave your skin feeling greasy. That’s what makes a gel moisturizer like this one so valuable during the summer. Add in aloe vera and green tea—two of the best ingredients at helping skin recover from sun exposure—and you’ve got yourself the perfect solution to long, sunny days.

Testing Notes: As mentioned above, I can get awfully red. This is especially true after extended sun exposure, no matter how diligent I am with sunscreen. Last summer I started using the Versed Dew Point Gel Moisturizer, and it’s been my secret weapon during the warmer months ever since. It feels silky and cooling on my face, absorbing in seconds, while minimizing any inflammation that the daily UVs have created. Plus, it’s under $15, which makes this gel a serious bargain.

You don't need a moisturizer to be 100 percent natural or organic to be effective—some of the most proven skincare ingredients, including ceramides (barrier repair), niacinamide (brightening and redness reduction), glycerin (hydration), and hyaluronic acid (moisture retention), are often lab-made and highly effective at supporting healthy, hydrated skin. But if your skin tends to appreciate more natural formulas, or you want something a bit more environmentally friendly, Jackfir is the ideal choice.

It’s boosted by natural skin-loving ingredients like squalane, aloe, mushroom, niacinamide, and vitamin C, creating a lightweight moisturizer that delivers lasting hydration and a healthy skin barrier. It’s even EWG Verified—meaning it’s proven to be transparent with its ingredients—and made with at least 70 percent organic ingredients.

Testing Notes: This cream absorbs quickly with no greasy feel and even helps soothe post-shave irritation, not a huge surprise, as the brand is responsible for my best overall shave cream. Beyond the soothing feel, it features a relaxing, earthy scent that doesn’t irritate my skin (which can be sensitive to fragrances) and helps support its organic-focused formula.

As someone who cares about the planet, I also appreciate that a portion of all Jackfir sales goes toward planting trees. It’s a bit pricier, sure, but this stuff lasts because you only need to use a little at a time to cover your entire face. Using it twice daily, I get close to three months out of one tube. When my beard is longer and covers the lower half of my face, I can stretch it even further.

Understanding your skin type is essential for choosing the right moisturizer. Sure, but how do you identify your skin type? Focus on the T-zone, which is the area across your forehead and down the center of your face. At the end of the day, check this area in the mirror to see how it looks and feels, keeping an eye out for the following signs.

According to dermatologist Dr. Joshua Zeichner, M.D., moisturizers primarily rely on three types of ingredients: occlusives, humectants, and emollients. Your skin type determines which you should zero in on. They break down like this.

As a grooming editor, I am constantly testing moisturizers, including the latest innovations and releases. I have normal to dry skin, which can also be quite sensitive and prone to acne, so I’m able to test a wide range of moisturizers for most skin types other than oily. In fact, I write a bi-monthly column detailing my favorite new releases in grooming across all categories, and moisturizers often make the cut. For this story, I collected a group of my all-time favorites, past and present, to reevaluate over the past year-plus on their ingredients, feel, consistency, and long-term effectiveness.

That being said, I am far from the only one at Men’s Health who takes skincare seriously (our office is like #boybathroom gone wild). I also considered the go-to picks of fellow editors and writers, who have been testing moisturizers since our grooming vertical first launched in 2018. I especially considered recommendations for those with oily skin, to cover all skin type bases.

Finally, I presented the extensive list of moisturizers that saw positive results to a panel of dermatologists to ensure every entry was effective and safe, while inquiring about which they recommend to their patients. With all this in mind, I narrowed our list to the ten best moisturizers for men with any skin type, be it dry, oily, sensitive, or somewhere in between.

Men need to moisturize every day—full stop. This is regardless of skin type, as even oily and acne-prone skin needs the added benefits of a moisturizing product to help regulate sebum production, according to dermatologist Dr. Corey L. Hartman, M.D. No matter your skin type, you should apply a moisturizer twice daily—once in the morning and once at night.

Moisturizer should always be the last or second-to-last step in your routine. They’re designed to not only impart hydration to your skin but also lock in the moisture that it already has, as well as the ingredients in any other products you’ve used.

An easy way to remember it is this: No matter how many products you’re using, you want to layer them from thinnest to thickest textures. After cleansing, apply any serums or other thinner products before sealing them all in with your moisturizer. In the morning, you’ll want to top the moisturizer with sunscreen, but at night, you can just end with your moisturizer.

A lot of guys skip moisturizing because they hate how it feels—greasy, heavy, or sticky formulas are instant dealbreakers. The good news? Moisturizers come in all forms, including gels, which pack high water content for fast absorption and a clean, non-tacky finish, according to dermatologist Dr. Estee Williams, M.D.

Your choice should match your skin type—gels work best for oily skin, while thicker creams suit dry patches—but the key is picking a moisturizer you actually want to use every day. If it’s just gathering dust on your shelf, it’s doing nothing for your skin.

Dermatologist Dr. Sarah Stierman, M.D., recommends using multi-tasking moisturizers that include niacinamide, which fights inflammation and prevents blemishes in oily skin; hyaluronic acid, which attracts and locks in moisture; and ceramides, which repair the skin barrier and soothe the skin, crucial for anyone who shaves regularly.

#5136. What to Wear to Thanksgiving: 6 Outfit Ideas for Every Type of Gathering

From dressier holiday looks to comfy and stretchy.

Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

With Thanksgiving just around the corner, I’ve already started thinking about two very important things: what’s going on the dinner table and what I’ll wear. I’m especially looking forward to my mom’s baked mashed potatoes (a family favorite) and the homemade mac and cheese I’ll be bringing along. But, especially as a style writer, half the fun of the holidays is having a good excuse to put together a good outfit.

My family’s Thanksgiving gatherings tend to be pretty casual, so I’m not one to show up in anything overly dressy or uncomfortable. I’m usually somewhere in the middle, opting for an outfit that looks like I made an effort but still lets me enjoy a second helping of stuffing without worrying about a too-tight waistband. Think a great sweater with loose-fitting jeans, a knit dress with boots, or even a smartly-styled leggings outfit. Because as much as I love dressing up for the holidays, I also want to enjoy post-dinner card games or sit comfortably on the couch afterward.

If you’re approaching Thanksgiving dressing the same way, I’ve rounded up six outfit ideas to help get you inspired. I’ve included a few options perfect for a Christmas card photoshoot, along with more laid-back looks that are just as fitting for a casual family gathering. No matter what your holiday plans look like, these outfits strike that happy medium between looking good and feeling comfortable. Now, if you’ll excuse me, I have some mac and cheese to make.

In my opinion, there’s no outfit more perfect for the holidays than a sweater dress and boots. It’s cute enough for family photos but loose and soft enough to keep you comfy all day (especially if you kick the boots off at the door). Grab a long-sleeve knit dress that hits somewhere between mid-thigh and the knee and pair it with some fleece-lined tights and your fave knee-high boot. A midi or maxi dress with an ankle bootie works too.

Start by pulling out a denim jacket and denim skirt. From there, add a plain white T-shirt. I love brown for the fall, so I wore my version of this outfit with brown boots and a matching brown belt and bag. I love this combo because it looks super stylish, but I don’t feel overdressed or uncomfortable when I wear it. Don’t have a denim skirt or jacket? No problem. You can recreate this look with a leather jacket, jeans, or any neutral mini skirt.

Start with a pair of satin or silk pants and pair them with a sweater and ballet flats in the same shade. This outfit has been one of my go-tos lately because it’s so comfortable, but the monochrome palette and shiny finish of the pants make it look like I tried way harder than I actually did. You can even make it feel a little dressier by swapping the flats for a pair of pointed-toe ankle boots.

It doesn’t get comfier than leggings and slippers. For ultra-casual gatherings when you just want to focus on family and food without looking frumpy, just style yours a little smarter. Go for a pair of leggings with minimal seaming (especially a pair without a front seam), which makes them look sleeker. Then grab a dressy-looking oversized sweater—something with a boxy cut, a turtleneck, or a nice knit. I find that my tweed stitch J. Crew Rollneck Sweater is perfect for this look. Finish it off with a neutral slipper and a pair of scrunchy socks.

Crz Yoga SculptAir No Front Seam Leggings

Opt for a pair of baggier jeans for this more casual outfit, which will be way comfier than a restrictive skinny or straight-leg jean. A looser pant also pairs better with a cozy boot, like this platform ankle boot. Finally, throw on a long-sleeve top or sweater with a cute vest for an outfit that feels very fall.

Banana Republic The Icon Classic Wide-Leg Jean

Okay, you caught me—I actually wore this outfit for Christmas last year instead of Thanksgiving, but it definitely works for either holiday! For this combo, start with your favorite skirt and a turtleneck top. Then top it off with a relaxed-fitting blazer (I love this houndstooth blazer, but any pattern or solid color will do). On the bottom, throw on a pair of tights and a knee-high boot.

#5134. Aave’s $4 billion USDC borrow cap could leave just $190 million available for withdrawals

One wallet supplied more than a billion USDC to Aave’s Ethereum pool. The $190 million scenario assumes borrowing reaches the new cap and deposits stay at Friday’s level.

Aave raised its USDC borrow cap in the main Ethereum V3 market to $4 billion on Nov. 20, a day after one wallet deposited more than a billion USDC. Lenders had about 1.14 billion USDC available to withdraw late on Nov. 20. If borrowing hits the new cap and deposits stay at 4.19 billion USDC, about 190 million USDC would remain for withdrawals.

Aave's Ethereum Core market had 4.19 billion USDC supplied and 3.05 billion borrowed at 22:11 UTC on Nov. 20, according to an Aave API snapshot published by Aave Tracker. With 72.8% of the reserve lent out, subtracting the loans leaves about 1.14 billion USDC unborrowed. The same figures put borrowers about 950 million USDC below the new cap. That gap measures room under the borrowing limit.

The address, 0x176F…a132, supplied 400 million USDC and 350 million USDC in two transactions about eight minutes apart on Nov. 19. The same wallet received Aave's receipt tokens from both deposits.

Later that day, Aave raised the market's USDC deposit limit from 3.5 billion to 5 billion. LlamaRisk had reported that the old limit was 99.6% used. Four minutes and 24 seconds after the change, the same wallet supplied another 738 million USDC, bringing its deposits to 1,488 million USDC over about 75 minutes.

Coindaro reported that at 17:43 UTC on Nov. 19 the wallet held about 1.495 billion in aEthUSDC, the token that represents its deposits and accrued interest. At that same reading, the market had 4.228 billion USDC supplied and 2.604 billion borrowed, leaving roughly 1.62 billion unborrowed. At Ethereum block 26,459,205, just before 22:11 UTC on Nov. 20, on-chain balances showed the address holding about 1.495 billion aEthUSDC, or 35.7% of the receipt token's supply.

LlamaRisk recommended the higher borrowing limit on Nov. 20 after loans reached 98.5% of the previous $2.7 billion cap. Aave put the change into effect at 11:15 UTC. The amount of cash in the pool changes when users actually borrow, deposit, repay or withdraw.

At the late Nov. 20 supply of 4.19 billion USDC, the pool would have about 690 million left with 3.5 billion borrowed and 190 million left with 4 billion borrowed. The latter would put utilization at about 95.5%, above the 94% threshold where the variable borrowing rate starts to rise more steeply.

LlamaRisk's earlier numbers put the full-cap buffer slightly higher. The firm estimated that $4 billion of debt would use 94.8% of the supply at the time of its recommendation, implying roughly 220 million USDC unborrowed. If deposits eventually reached the $5 billion supply cap, the same $4 billion of debt would leave 1 billion USDC in the pool.

Aave pays withdrawals from the USDC still available in the pool. At the late Nov. 20 reading, the wallet's roughly 1.495 billion USDC position exceeded the pool's estimated 1.14 billion of unborrowed USDC. A hypothetical 500 million USDC withdrawal at that reading, with debt held at 3.05 billion, would leave about 640 million for other suppliers. The same request would exceed the pool's liquidity in the $4 billion debt scenario. As the cash balance falls, so does the share of that wallet's position it could redeem at once.

Transferring aEthUSDC to a new holder would move the claim on the deposit. Redeeming it would take USDC out of the pool. How much other lenders can withdraw depends on the size of those redemptions and whether repayments or fresh deposits replenish the pool as loans grow.

#5133. The Best Men's Travel Blazers in 2026, Tested by Style Editors

Our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

Silhouettes from Uniqlo, Suitsupply, and Eddie Bauer went the distance in our testing.

WHETHER YOU’RE PACKING for a trip or just gearing up for a long commute, keeping a travel blazer in your rotation saves you time—and a lot of outfit stress. When you’re bouncing from one to the next with no time to reset, this is the one piece in your wardrobe that won’t fall apart. Unlike traditional blazers, these travel styles resist wrinkles, breathe easily, and have enough stretch that you still feel comfortable during those cramped flights and shoulder-to-shoulder train rides. On top of that, they’re easy to pack in your luggage and pair with a bunch of ensembles.

Since 2022, we’ve tested over 25 travel blazers, seeing how they hold up in overhead bins, on sweaty commutes, and straight out of a bag. The best ones are tailored, not restrictive, lightweight but not flimsy, and polished without feeling overdone. No one’s traveling in a three-piece suit anymore. Here are the best travel blazers to get you through it all.

In the past year, our style team has tested dozens of travel blazers for functionality and Relwen has it in spades. Right off the bat, we noticed that its cotton-spandex fabric feels super lightweight and comes with enough stretch to let you move beyond limitations. It leans more sport jacket with a four-button design and throat latch that allows you to button all the way up to your neck. There are also functional buttons on the sleeves, which look sharp rolled up. I’ve worn it in low 50s as well as high 70s, and found it to be comfortable in both temps.

Normally, I have to pay to dry clean most of my blazers, but this one can be tossed around my washing machine without falling apart. As for storage, the three exterior patch pockets are similar to any casual blazer, but the large interior pocket has a zip closure with a vertical opening for easy access. It is ideal for stashing valuables.

On top of being a solid choice for away seminars or long flights, this option is great for everyday wear. It looks great during cool evening strolls, dinner dates, and outdoor weddings. Sure, this blazer gets wrinkled easily, but it’s designed to give off a laid-back vibe, as if it’s been worn and broken in over time.

In Rhone’s vast assortment, the brand carries a travel blazer with a killer slim cut. It has a sporty vibe, but looks clean enough for meetings that aren’t too formal. The Flex-Knit fabric is breathable and moisture-wicking, which means you stay cool and the garment doesn’t become damp or develop unpleasant odors from sweat. The polyester material has plenty of stretch, so I never felt any restriction in the arm area when I grabbed my coffee or reached up to the high cabinet.

I’ve paired it with everything from a basic tee to an oxford shirt, and it looks great with just about anything in your wardrobe—a true testament to its versatility. Plus, the material is ultra-light, making it a comfortable pick to throw on. Unlike Relwen’s travel blazer, this one can’t go in the washer—you have to take a trip to the dry cleaners.

Eddie Bauer’s travel blazer is practically indestructible. The fabric is hardcore and can take a beating, thanks to the reinforced seams and durable water-repellent finish. The latter especially makes sure you’re covered if you spill a drink or get caught in a downpour. And when you’re commuting, you can secure your passport or phone inside zippered compartments.

During our testing, we found that the two-way stretch made a journey a breeze, giving us the freedom to move through busy airports and crowded streets. Plus, the universal fit hits the sweet spot, so it’s comfortable for all body types without being too tight or too loose.

Although Uniqlo’s design looks like a wool blazer replica, it’s one of the most breathable styles I’ve ever worn. It’s made with the brand’s proprietary AirSense fabric, a lightweight polyester material that dries in minutes and keeps me cool. Typically, when I wear a traditional blazer in the summertime and in the muggy subway, I sweat like a dog. But when I wore this one in 80-degree weather to a work brunch, I was comfortable and dry the whole time. It’s relaxed enough to wear with chinos or jeans, but still has a dressy vibe that can pull off a full-suit look with trousers.

I found it’s not too fitted in the waist, which lets me layer shirts or knits easier in the cooler temps. There’s no bunching to where I feel stuffed. You can snag it in the typical neutral colors like gray and navy, perfect for the office followed by dinner plans. Like Relwen’s offering, this one is machine washable, but I recommend turning it inside out in a mesh bag. On the other hand, it’s way more structured with a natural shaping in the shoulders and sleeves. And yeah, it’s the most affordable option on this list, clocking in under $100, but it doesn’t look or feel like a budget buy. You’re getting the same premium quality that you’d get with a blazer that cost a few hundred bucks.

In an effort to max out comfort, Faherty offers a travel blazer made out of a stretch jersey knit fabric. It has a soft hand feel, tailored fit, and wears like your coziest cardigan. The front pockets are deep enough to carry your earbuds or wallet, so either won’t fall out as you’re maneuvering through the airport. Whether you’re packing it all in a backpack or suitcase, it’s a breeze to toss in and hit the road. Plus, we found no signs of wrinkles after unloading our clothes in the hotel.

Unlike stiff travel blazers that we’ve tested, this one bends and moves with you, so it doesn’t feel like you’re stuck in a straightjacket. The slimmer cut is perfect for guys who have an athletic or lean build, as it accentuates a trim silhouette and creates a sharp appearance. It’s a perfect match with a pair of summer pants, but looks just as cool with jeans and a tee.

When you want to look like you mean business at client dinners or conferences, you should reach for this blazer from Hugo Boss. Most travel blazers prioritize comfort at the expense of polish, but this one manages to deliver both. Our Style and Reviews Director Christian Gollayan loves how sharp this slim-fit silhouette looks on him. He says it's tailored without feeling restrictive, while the stretch-infused, polyester-wool fabric gives you enough mobility for long flights and days spent hauling luggage through airports. The biggest differentiator, though, is right in the name: it’s washable. I can wear it repeatedly on a multi-day trip, freshen it up without a costly dry-cleaning bill, and pack it with far less anxiety than a traditional wool sport coat.

I wore the jacket on a full travel day that included a flight, a lengthy commute, and several hours seated at meetings. It kept its shape surprisingly well, resisting the creases and rumpling that typically throw off more formal tailoring after being folded inside a carry-on. What impressed me most was how effortlessly it transitioned from travel wear to evening attire. I could step off a plane and head directly to a dinner reservation without feeling underdressed. Admittedly, the jacket isn’t as soft or unstructured as more casual travel blazers from performance-focused brands. Also, the slimmer cut may feel less forgiving if you prefer a relaxed fit. But if your priority is maintaining a clean, business-ready vibe while still getting travel-friendly performance, I haven’t found many options that strike the balance as well as this one.

If you’re looking for a travel blazer that leans more dressy with European tailoring and luxurious quality for a great price point, Suitsupply is your best bet. Instead of a boxy, rigid silhouette that’s on trend right now, this timeless design has a natural shoulder, single-breasted closure, and a half-canvas construction that helps the jacket mold to your body over time while maintaining a solid drape.

It’s made with medium weight pure wool, but I wasn’t burning up wearing it with a tank top at a rooftop party. When the temperature really spikes beyond 80 degrees, I would recommend reaching for something lighter like linen. The chest and waist is trimmed for a slim fit, but it’s not too tight in the arms. I wore a 36R and didn’t need any alteration. It looks sharp straight off the rack. Sure, it’s on the pricier end compared to other picks on the list, but you’ll have this blazer for seasons to come. You can wear it to the office, formal business events, or weddings.

Linen blazers, like this one by Charles Tyrwhitt, reign supreme for travel because I stay cool, dry, and comfortable. Even though this design’s fabric blends cotton and linen, you’re still getting a hefty dose of linen (53%), so it wears as light as a feather. As I’m commuting, airflow is constant, and it never feels stuffy like wool, even when the temps spike. Linen is notorious for wrinkling, but this one’s got enough structure that creases barely register—and the taupe color blends in, helping to mask any wrinkles that do show up.

The cut is relaxed through the chest and waist, with a clean, structured drape that follows the body without pulling. The shoulders are lightly structured, giving you shape up top without feeling stiff. It’s a sharper silhouette overall, but still works for guys with broader shoulders or a bigger chest. But if you’re on the leaner side, it captures that close-to-the-body, tailored look.

If you want a blazer that feels like a step up from your usual travel uniform, I would highly consider this number from Bonobos. Unlike stiff, restrictive blazers that make you feel like you’re trapped in a straightjacket, this cotton-spandex blend flexes with you, whether you’re reaching for your luggage in the overhead bin or hailing a cab. I have to admit, it does wrinkle quite a bit when I’m sitting down for a long amount of time. In true Bonobos fashion, this blazer comes in three fits—slim, athletic, and standard—so every guy can find his perfect match. And it’s far more relaxed than a traditional sport coat. Just a note: you can only take it to the dry cleaners. In terms of styling, it’s super versatile: you can wear it with a dress shirt and chinos for a garden party or a casual T-shirt and jeans for a laid-back look on your next trip.

Read more: Bonobos Jetsetter Blazer Review

If I’m traveling somewhere warm and still want to look put-together, Buck Mason’s carry-on blazer is the one I keep coming back to. Its cotton-linen blend combines the breathability of pure linen along with the durability and structure of cotton. You get that relaxed, cool texture that makes linen so comfortable in the summer, but without the excessive wrinkling that can make traditional linen jackets look disheveled halfway through a trip.

What I liked most was how well it handled repeated packing and unpacking. While it picked up some natural creasing—as any linen-rich garment will—it never looked sloppy. The cotton component helped the jacket retain its shape, while the linen kept it noticeably cooler than traditional wool tailoring during warm afternoons. At 5’8”, I also appreciated that the silhouette felt tailored without being overly structured or stiff. The jacket’s biggest strength is versatility. It pairs just as naturally with chinos and loafers for a dinner reservation as it does with shorts and minimal sneakers for a day of sightseeing.

Unlike performance travel blazers that can sometimes look overly technical, the Capitola leans into classic menswear styling with a fabric that develops character the more you wear it. It’s not the blazer I’d choose for highly formal business settings, but for warm-weather travel, it’s one of the most wearable options I’ve tested.

When shopping for men’s travel blazers, look for fabrics that are comfy and practical. Men’s travel blazers are built to look like traditional blazers, while providing the feel and function of athletic outerwear. Go for stretchy materials like spandex or elastane, so you can move without any hassle or restriction. Wrinkle-resistant materials like polyester or blends are great because they remain looking sharp after you unravel them from your suitcase. Breathable materials like cotton and lightweight wool keep you cool and comfortable.

Make sure your blazer fits well and is comfortable enough to wear all day. Travel blazers for men should allow freedom of movement and not feel too tight or restrictive. The shoulders of the garment need to align with your own and not sag or pinch, as this affects the overall look. Always double-check the sleeves; see that they’re not too long and the armholes are high enough to avoid bunching while allowing mobility. When it comes to travel blazers, you'll typically find these three main types of fits.

A more tailored cut that's snug around the chest and waist, giving you a sharp, sleek silhouette. Great for guys who want a more fitted look without sacrificing comfort.

A fit that's perfect for guys with broader shoulders and a smaller waist. It offers more room in the chest and shoulders, while still tapering at the waist for a streamlined look.

The classic, relaxed fit. It offers more room throughout the body and is great for a laid-back, comfortable look. Ideal for guys who prioritize freedom of movement and a less structured feel.

A packable travel blazer can easily be folded or rolled up if it's taking too much space in your luggage, leaving room for other essentials. Having one that packs well means you can just throw it in the bag and go, making your travel preparations simpler and more efficient.

Check for practical features like multiple pockets for easy access to essentials and moisture-wicking properties if you intend to be active.

To find the best travel blazers for men, our style team led by Style and Reviews Director Christian Gollayan, tested dozens over the past few years. We wore them during business conferences, day trips, and leisure vacations. We tested each one, checking to see which allowed for easy movement, felt light, and fit nicely throughout the body. We also analyzed the packing process and styled the blazer with different outfits to make sure it worked for both casual and formal settings. We then narrowed down to the eight best travel blazers for men that give you a stylish and refined look that attracts only the best kind of attention.

Think of your travel blazer more like a lightweight jacket. Any blazer in a dark, neutral color or simple pattern can go on top of pretty much any outfit. Whether you wear a button-down shirt or a hoodie, throwing a blazer over it instantly levels up your look. Alas, we tend to not use the pockets of suits or formal blazers very often, but you should utilize all the pocket space of travel blazers.

#5131. The 7 Best Facial Hair Removal Tools, Tested by Editors

Walk don’t run to Amazon because our best overall recommendation is 26% off RN.

Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

There are tons of different facial hair removal methods for women, including laser hair removal, waxing, and epilators. I have tried them all, including electric razors and dermaplaning tools. As WH’s beauty editor, I've sugared my face and body and interviewed dozens of derms about preventing dreaded razor bumps and unsightly ingrown hairs. Some facial hair removal methods take only a few minutes, while others can be pretty painful but require minimal upkeep. Finding the right method or combination of methods that work for your needs might take a few tries, but I've got you covered with my beauty editor-vetted recommendations. These editor-tested and dermatologist-recommended suggestions start at just $10.

Yes, this is the priciest recommendation, but it's totally worth the splurge. Braun works in just one treatment session and boasts smart features that justify the added cost and our top spot. The results are immediate, long-lasting, and include three attachments for the face, bikini line, and rest of the body.

Skin i·expert is Braun’s only laser made with a proprietary SensoAdapt technology that scans your skin tone and automatically adjusts the light intensity for an effective and safer hair removal experience. The software is controlled with the Braun smartphone app. It also sends alerts when you missed a spot, used the wrong device head, applied too much pressure, or used it too quickly.

Wohlner relies on this device every few weeks to remove her self-described "super coarse hair." Since laser hair removal isn't permanent, some hairs will still pop up. However, they grow back slower, which is a major win for Wohlner.

Laser hair removal also gets a pretty bad rep for being painful. While the Braun isn't equipped with any cooling sensation to relieve discomfort, the pain is relatively mild. "I felt a little zippiness here and there, but nothing I could actually describe as painful—more like a super quick, tiny pinch," says Wohlner.

As for the results, they were solid. Wohlner didn't have to shave her hair for weeks after the first treatment, and three sessions later, her hair regrowth slowed down. The upfront cost is pricey, but it'll save you from purchasing expensive pro-grade appointments and allow you to remove hair whenever and wherever you choose.

Read More: Electrolysis Versus Laser Hair Removal

Finishing Touch is an underrated brand. I previously included the brand’s electric shaver with a built-in LED ring light to illuminate hairs I wouldn't usually see in my bathroom. However, it’s no longer being sold and cost more than double the price. This slimmer version is the ideal facial hair removal tool for budget-conscious shoppers, and I wish I ordered mine sooner.

I can achieve similar results using razors three times the price. The Flawless device is also so much prettier than boring razors. The rose gold hair remover is rather discreet and looks similar to dermaplaning tool. It features a small head that contours along the curves of my face, while the blade ensures I have the smoothest trim.

This device works great if you have sensitive skin that's easily irritated. It's gentle enough to use daily, and I love keeping mine on hand at the office to check my face before walking into a meeting.

The only caveat is Flawless is a razor, so it cuts hair at the top layer of skin, meaning hair will grow back relatively fast. So, as long as you don't mind regular trims, this is an epic choice.

After two years of on-and-off testing, Flamingo still makes my favorite razor. Its sharp blades that don’t tug or pull at my sensitive skin elevate Flamingo to the top of my shower routine.

The brand suggests replacing the blades every four to six weeks, but each blade lasts me closer to eight weeks, meaning a regular four-pack of blades lasts me approximately 32 weeks (eight months) before becoming dull. Plus, this razor set is comfy to use while shaving down to my ankles. It curves along my kneecaps and pits with ease, and it hasn’t caused any nicks or ingrown hairs along my bikini line.

I’ll continue using Flamingo, and at just $16, you can also enjoy smooth skin which includes the razor, four blades, and a holder that fits neatly in cramped spaces like my New York City shower.

While I don't mind using a traditional manual razor or dermaplaning, it's worth spending a little extra on this electric device, says Wohlner. This Philips electric razor has a large head and self-sharpening blade to rapidly remove facial hair. Wohlner's been using this facial hair removal tool for hairs and considers it the most effective method for eliminating stubborn upper lip and chin hairs. "While it's too big to remove hair on my brows, it's awesome for those larger areas of the face when you're short on time and want to look smooth and stubble-free," she says.

Many other tools can irritate, especially around the upper lip area, which occasionally turns into bumps. This shaver has a hypoallergenic stainless steel head that doesn’t irritate sensitive skin, quickly removing unwanted hair in a single pass without causing pain or discomfort. This device keeps Wohlner's face smooth, and it always glides over the skin effortlessly without leaving it red and raw. It even comes with a built-in mirror in the cap to touch-up on the go.

Pro tip: The large shaver head does tend to get clogged after a few uses, which can be prevented if you wipe it down with alcohol after every use. Taking care of your device will ensure you get the closest shave and that it lasts for years.

The idea of gliding a sharp razor across my face was initially intimidating, but I haven't scratched myself since using the Dermaflash. Unlike cheaper options with dull blades, the Dermaflash provides the most professional-grade shave I've ever experienced while testing dozens of dermaplaning tools. The sharp blade features proprietary Microfine Edges, which are tiny corrugations that get super close to my face without any discomfort.

Most dermaplaning tools only have simple blades, but Dermaflash features a gentle pulsing technology that further removes peach fuzz and dead skin cells instantly and safely, making it handy for beginners and seasoned dermaplaning users alike. My results rival pro treatments without the hassle of going to a spa and without the excessive upkeep cost. This tool easily glides across my face, which would normally be a challenge with cheaper, manual dermaplaning tools. Since using this device, I noticed my face cream sinks in quickly, and my foundation looks even more natural.

I try to use this tool every two weeks to maintain my smooth results, but TBH, I use it monthly, which is better for my wallet. The brand advises swapping out the blade after every use for the smoothest results, so anything to stretch my beauty budget is always a win. FWIW: Even a monthly treatment prevents my makeup from pilling, so this tool will remain a consistent part of my routine.

Sugaring is epic because the paste only sticks to the hair, not the skin. It's far less painful than waxing and easier to apply.

I've previously only done professional sugaring, but the at-home process is the same. After heating the roller in the microwave, I apply the stick directly to the area I want sugared, lay down a strip, and pull it off in the opposite direction of the hair growth. The fabric strips are a little big to use on my face, especially on the chin or upper lip, but I can cut them in half, and they work perfectly.

Most sugaring wax is packaged in a tub that can tip over and cause a huge, sticky mess. Schick comes in a deodorant-like stick that easily rolls onto my skin. I like to warm the stick up in the microwave in 5-second increments until the paste has a honey-like consistency. I also need a light layer of sugaring wax to achieve the same results as other alternatives, meaning my roller can last for a few months.

I initially missed a few hairs, so I had to follow up with a fresh swipe of sugaring paste. With some practice, my technique improved over time, and soon enough, it only took me a few minutes to wax the lower half of my face. At just $13 a wand, this at-home technique is much cheaper than going to a salon where I'd easily pay double the price, and for that alone, I'll continue using this kit.

This hair removal cream isn't the Nair you grew up on. It's a prescription-strength cream specifically formulated to slow hair growth on the face. The key ingredients include eflornithine (6%), which blocks the enzyme ornithine decarboxylase (ODC) that stimulates hair growth. Each batch is compounded together shortly before shipping, ensuring maximum potency.

I've tried many hair removal creams, which sometimes cause redness and irritation, so I was worried Musely would be a problem. Musely provides instant hair-free results, and I noticed my regrowth is slower and my skin remains smoother with regular use, compared to other creams I’ve tried. It has a light tingling sensation, letting me know the cream is working. Unlike cheaper drugstore alternatives, Musely hasn't irritated my skin. It also doesn't have a super aggressive chemical smell like other alternatives I tested, and that alone is a win in my book.

The major downside of hair removal creams, including Musely, is that I have to adjust when I use my tretinoin prescription around hair removal days. After Musely hair removal, I typically wait a few days before safely applying my tretinoin cream. Otherwise, I might experience redness, irritation, and over-exfoliate my skin. Musely is a worthwhile product, but I prefer dermaplaning or shaving because I value acne-free skin over a fast-acting, pain-free hair removal process.

Your hair color, skin color, and hair thickness helps determine your best facial hair removal method, says dermatologist Blair Murphy-Rose, MD. Also be real about your pain tolerance and bandwidth because the best method for removing facial hair is the one you'll consistently use to maintain smooth results. Also, think about investing in an electric hair removal device to speed up your primping routine and, of course, stick to your budget. Our suggestions start at just $10.

They are epic when you have dark hair and a fair to medium complexion; particularly those with thick, coarse and unruly dark chin, upper lip, and sideburn hair. "This combination of hair color and skin tone ensures that the hairs alone are absorbing the majority of the laser energy," dermatologist Rachel Nazarian, MD,,, recently told WH.

But if you're a four or deeper on the Fitzpatrick Scale like me, you should skip using at-home laser hair removal devices. "You want to receive the right treatment that does not harm your skin," dermatologist Jeanine Downie, MD, previously told WH.

They work by slowing hair growth and reducing strand thickness by using highly concentrated light to penetrate hair follicles and inhibit future hair growth. While laser hair removal isn't exactly permanent, it can effectively slow hair growth. While the upfront cost is a tad of a jumpscare, these devices typically contain about 200,000 flashes, which is equivalent to 780 at-home treatments, says Dr. Nazarian.

This is my go-to hair removal method because of the low upkeep. I can easily go 4-6 weeks between my sessions, but TBH, I'll stretch it to every 8 weeks. It is relatively painful since it involves simultaneously removing dozens of hairs from the root, but it's a quick process and the results last longer than dermaplaning or shaving. I've been waxing for years and find the pain has become quite tolerable. On a scale of 1 to 10, waxing my face and underarms ranges from 2—3 and 4—6 elsewhere on my body, with the most painful spots being the back of my legs and bikini area. Sugaring It is similar to waxing but less painful. I've had some uncomfy waxes that stung my sensitive skin, but sugaring is noticeably milder. Ingredients will vary among brands, but there is almost always a mix of sugar, water, and lemon. The golden paste is molded onto your skin where you'd like to remove hair, and you'll gently remove it with a fast flicking technique like waxing.

These are tried-and-true hair removal tools that are cheap, readily accessible, and provide instant results. Your best bet is to use a razor with a non-slip ergonomic handle to keep your shave steady. I also like razors featuring a lubricating strip to help prevent irritation. Depending on how fast your facial hair regrows, you might need to shave daily or every few days, but they're pain-free. Remember to use shaving cream and gently run the blade in the opposite direction of hair growth. There are also manual and electric razors, but I'll discuss that more in the next section.

They feature surgical blades to remove dead skin cells and peach fuzz from your face. These devices also have long handles and sturdy grips to prevent accidental cuts. Because dermaplaning sloughs off dead skin cells, this hair removal tool provides the smoothest makeup application.

This method helps promote cell turnover and collagen production plus minimizes dark spots and uneven skin texture, dermatologist Azadeh Shirazi, MD, told WH. "When your skin is hairless and buildup-free, it looks super toned and bright," Dr. Shirazi said.

Since dermaplaning cuts the hairs at the top layer of skin, they'll grow back quicker than laser hair removal or waxing, says Dr. Murphy-Rose. So be ready to use this technique 1-4 times monthly, depending on how fast your hair regrows.

These creams typically contain ingredients like eflornithine, calcium hydroxide, calcium thioglycolate, sodium hydroxide, and sodium thioglycolate to dissolve keratin bond structures of strands, making them pain-free alternatives to tweezing, waxing, and sugaring. Let the cream sit for a few minutes, then wipe it away to reveal smoother skin. If your skin is super sensitive, you could leave it on for 1-3 minutes and then shave it off in warm water, dermatologist S. Manjula Jegasothy, MD, previously told us. Hair will begin to grow back within a few days, so you're looking at a low-key commitment.

These are best for removing hair from a small area of the face, like your eyebrows, chin, and upper lip. TBH, tweezing has mild to moderate discomfort since you're plucking hairs from the root. On a scale of 1—10, I'd rank the pain level from 4—6. Since I have sensitive eyes that easily water, I stay away from tweezing my brows, but I found plucking a rogue chin hair pretty mild. Upkeep depends on how fast your hair grows back. Some women want to pluck every few days, while others can stretch their tweezing schedule to every few weeks.

Dermaplaning tools and razors are either manual or electric powered by batteries or a USB or USB-C cable.

When you pick electric devices like the Dermaflash, you'll be spending around $200, while manual tools, including hair removal creams and razors are much cheaper. With prices ranging from $150 to $600, epilators and laser hair removal devices are definite investments, but still cost less than a series of professional sessions. Some of these splurge-worthy devices also have smart capabilities like Bluetooth, smartphone app features, and even calendar reminders to remove facial hair.

Ultimately, opt for the electric devices if you want a fast and powerful tool that lasts for years and don't mind the upfront cost. Choose a manual tool if you would rather save the cash for other beauty products, like an LED face mask or a red light therapy device for hair growth.

Keeping the above guidelines in mind—type, cost, and manual versus electric devices—I carefully researched dozens of at-home facial hair removal tools. After settling on 12 contenders, I spent several months testing and I was only truly impressed by a handful of picks. I evaluated their ease of use, how often I needed to remove hair, and how seamless they were to incorporate into my routine. I also consulted dermatologists and associate commerce editor Lily Wohlner, about her no-fail recommendations to share the best facial hair removal methods for women worth using in 2025.

Many at-home devices can’t distinguish between darker complexions and dark hair, dermatologist Dr. Nazarian previously told WH. Melanin-rich skin is at a higher risk of their skin absorbing laser hair and burning, said Dr. Nazarian. My advice: Either opt for a different alternative on this list or book an appointment with your dermatologist for specific guidance on the best laser hair removal treatment plan for you.
